chips.label: Instrumental
chips.prompt: instrumental, melody carried by the lead instrument
chips.desc: Flow's switch for a vocal-free track. Pair it with a named lead instrument (piano, sax, synth lead) so the melody has a clear voice.

chips.label: Solo female
chips.prompt: solo female lead vocal, clear and upfront in the mix
chips.desc: One female singer carries the song. Add a range and a tone chip (alto, soprano, breathy) so Flow picks a specific voice instead of a generic pop default.

chips.label: Solo male
chips.prompt: solo male lead vocal, warm and centered in the mix
chips.desc: One male singer carries the song. Add a range and a tone chip (baritone, tenor, raspy) to steer the exact voice.

chips.label: Male-female duet
chips.prompt: male and female duet, trading lines in the verses and harmonizing together on the chorus
chips.desc: Two leads in conversation. The classic shape for love songs, country duets, soul ballads and musical theater.

chips.label: Group / choir
chips.prompt: full mixed choir singing in rich four-part harmony, sopranos down to basses
chips.desc: Many voices in soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts. Adds weight to gospel, hymns, epic trailers and big pop finales.

chips.label: Child-like voice
chips.prompt: light, innocent child-like vocal with a sweet, pure and simple tone
chips.desc: A small, high, unforced voice. Useful for lullabies, nursery-rhyme pop, eerie horror cues and nostalgic indie.

chips.label: Androgynous
chips.prompt: androgynous lead vocal in the tenor-alto overlap, soft, smooth and gender-ambiguous
chips.desc: A voice that sits where high male and low female ranges meet. Common in synth-pop, art-pop, indie and alt R&B.

chips.label: Bass
chips.prompt: deep male bass vocal with a dark, rumbling low register and slow, steady phrasing
chips.desc: The lowest male voice, roughly E2 to E4. Brings gravitas to gospel quartets, doo-wop, dark folk and outlaw country.

chips.label: Baritone
chips.prompt: warm male baritone vocal with a rich, resonant chest tone in the low-mid range
chips.desc: The most common adult male range, about A2 to A4. Grounded and intimate; at home in country, crooner jazz, indie and rock.

chips.label: Tenor
chips.prompt: bright male tenor vocal that rings out in a high, clear upper range
chips.desc: The high male voice, roughly C3 to C5. Carries pop, rock and R&B choruses and cuts through dense mixes.

chips.label: Alto
chips.prompt: rich female alto vocal with a dusky, smoky lower register
chips.desc: The lowest common female range, about F3 to F5. Warm and earthy for jazz, soul, folk and moody pop.

chips.label: Mezzo-soprano
chips.prompt: expressive female mezzo-soprano vocal, full-bodied through the midrange with a bright top
chips.desc: The middle female voice, about A3 to A5. Versatile for musical theater, pop ballads and art song.

chips.label: Soprano
chips.prompt: clear high soprano vocal, pure and bell-like on the sustained top notes
chips.desc: The highest female voice, about C4 to C6. Light, floating and angelic in pop, choral, folk and cinematic music.

chips.label: Airy falsetto
chips.prompt: airy, weightless falsetto vocal floating high above the mix
chips.desc: A light head-voice register, most striking from male singers. A signature of neo-soul, disco, falsetto R&B and dreamy indie.

chips.label: Raspy / gravelly
chips.prompt: raspy, gravelly lead vocal with gritty texture and a worn, lived-in edge
chips.desc: Natural distortion in the voice itself. Sells blues, Southern rock, country and whiskey-soaked soul.

chips.label: Breathy
chips.prompt: breathy, intimate female vocal with soft air on every phrase, sung close to the mic
chips.desc: Lots of air and very little push. The sound of bedroom pop, trip-hop, slow R&B and dream pop.

chips.label: Smooth silky
chips.prompt: smooth, silky lead vocal with effortless legato phrasing and a polished tone
chips.desc: Even, controlled and glossy. Fits quiet-storm R&B, smooth jazz and adult contemporary.

chips.label: Powerful belting
chips.prompt: powerful belted lead vocal, full chest voice driving big sustained high notes
chips.desc: A loud, chest-dominant sound that carries over a full band. Use it for diva pop, power ballads, gospel and musical theater climaxes.

chips.label: Whispered
chips.prompt: hushed, whispered vocal delivered softly right at the listener's ear
chips.desc: Near-silent, close and ASMR-like. Great for dark pop verses, horror cues and intimate intros.

chips.label: Nasal indie
chips.prompt: slightly nasal, deadpan indie vocal with a casual, conversational tone
chips.desc: Unpolished and personal rather than virtuosic. Classic for indie rock, slacker rock, garage rock and lo-fi pop.

chips.label: Operatic
chips.prompt: operatic vocal with classical vibrato, projected resonance and soaring dramatic phrasing
chips.desc: Trained classical singing. Adds grandeur to symphonic metal, epic trailers, film scores and crossover pop.

chips.label: Soulful with runs
chips.prompt: soulful lead vocal with melismatic runs, blue-note bends and gospel-tinged embellishments
chips.desc: Many notes sung on a single syllable, with feeling. The core of R&B, gospel and neo-soul ballads.

chips.label: Fast-flow rap
chips.prompt: rapid-fire rap verses with dense, tightly packed syllables and crisp diction
chips.desc: Double-time delivery that packs four or more syllables into each beat. Shows off technique in battle rap, drill and grime.

chips.label: Melodic rap
chips.prompt: melodic rap vocal that half-sings verses and hooks with a sing-song cadence
chips.desc: The blend of rapping and singing that dominates modern hip-hop. Lines follow a melody but keep a rap rhythm.

chips.label: Triplet flow
chips.prompt: rap verses in a rolling triplet flow, three even syllables to every beat
chips.desc: Three syllables per beat laid over a straight trap groove. The bouncy cadence that defined 2010s Southern trap.

chips.label: Spoken word
chips.prompt: spoken-word vocal performed as rhythmic poetry over the music
chips.desc: Speech rather than song, with a poet's timing. Works for intros, interludes, trip-hop and cinematic hip-hop.

chips.label: Crooning
chips.prompt: smooth crooning vocal, relaxed and close with gentle vibrato
chips.desc: Soft, intimate singing made possible by the microphone. Think 1940s-50s ballads, lounge jazz and retro pop.

chips.label: Call and response
chips.prompt: call-and-response vocals, a lead line answered by a group reply
chips.desc: A leader sings a phrase and others answer it. Rooted in gospel, blues, soul, Afrobeat and work songs.

chips.label: Gang vocals / chants
chips.prompt: shouted gang vocals and crowd chants on the hook
chips.desc: Many voices shouting together in unison. Instant energy for punk, pop-punk, stadium rock and sports anthems.

chips.label: Stacked harmonies
chips.prompt: lush stacked vocal harmonies layered in thirds and fifths on the chorus
chips.desc: The same singer multitracked into chords. Gives choruses width and shine in pop, soft rock, R&B and K-pop.

chips.label: Ad-libs
chips.prompt: energetic background ad-libs punctuating the ends of lines
chips.desc: Short shouts, words and sounds around the main vocal. Essential flavor in trap and hip-hop, and in R&B outros.

chips.label: Auto-tuned melodic
chips.prompt: auto-tuned melodic vocal with hard pitch correction and glossy, robotic slides between notes
chips.desc: Pitch correction pushed until it becomes an audible effect. The signature vocal of trap, hyperpop, Afrobeats and modern pop.

chips.label: Vocoder
chips.prompt: robotic vocoder vocal carried by warm synth chords
chips.desc: A voice imposed onto a synthesizer so it sings in chords. Classic in electro-funk, French house, synth-pop and disco.

chips.label: Chopped vocal samples
chips.prompt: chopped, pitched vocal samples played rhythmically as a lead instrument
chips.desc: Single syllables sliced and played like a synth. A hallmark of future bass, house, UK garage and tropical house.

chips.label: Gospel ad-libs
chips.prompt: gospel ad-libs and soaring runs answering the lead, with a backing choir swelling behind
chips.desc: Improvised praise-style lines over the final choruses. Lifts gospel, soul and big pop ballads to a climax.

chips.label: Yodel-like flips
chips.prompt: yodel-like vocal flips snapping quickly between chest voice and head voice
chips.desc: Quick register breaks used as ornament. Heard in alpine folk, old-time country and quirky art-pop.

chips.label: Scat
chips.prompt: playful jazz scat singing, improvised syllables trading phrases with the band
chips.desc: Wordless improvised singing that imitates a horn solo. Classic in swing, bebop and vocal jazz.

chips.label: English
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in English
chips.desc: The default vocal language. Put English lyrics after a Lyrics: header and tag each section.

chips.label: Spanish
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in Spanish
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. Natural for reggaeton, Latin pop, salsa, bachata and regional Mexican styles.

chips.label: Portuguese
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in Portuguese
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. The voice of bossa nova, samba, MPB, sertanejo and fado.

chips.label: French
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in French
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. Suits chanson, French pop, cafe jazz and French rap.

chips.label: German
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in German
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. Fits synth-pop, schlager, industrial rock and German-language rap.

chips.label: Hindi
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in Hindi
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. Fits film-song ballads, Hindi pop, ghazal-inspired love songs and desi hip-hop.

chips.label: Japanese
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in Japanese
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. At home in J-pop, city pop, anime openings and J-rock.

chips.label: Korean
chips.prompt: lead vocals sung in Korean
chips.desc: A supported vocal language. The core of K-pop, K-R&B, ballads and Korean hip-hop, often with English hook lines.

chips.label: Intro
chips.prompt: atmospheric eight-bar intro that states the main motif before the groove enters
chips.desc: Sets the mood and key before anything else. Keep it to 4 to 8 bars for streaming; make it longer for DJ or film use.

chips.label: Verse
chips.prompt: understated verses with a lighter groove that leaves room for the vocal story
chips.desc: The storytelling sections. Lyrics change each time while the arrangement stays a step below the chorus.

chips.label: Pre-chorus
chips.prompt: rising pre-chorus that lifts the melody and builds tension into the chorus
chips.desc: A short ramp, often 4 to 8 bars, that changes chords and climbs so the chorus lands harder.

chips.label: Chorus / hook
chips.prompt: big, memorable chorus hook with the fullest arrangement, returning after every verse
chips.desc: The emotional and commercial center of a song: same words each time, highest energy, and usually the title line.

chips.label: Post-chorus
chips.prompt: chant-like post-chorus with a repeated vocal or synth tag right after the hook
chips.desc: A second, simpler hook straight after the chorus. Common in modern pop, K-pop and EDM-pop.

chips.label: Bridge
chips.prompt: contrasting bridge with new chords and a stripped-back texture before the last chorus
chips.desc: Fresh harmony or a new perspective, usually heard once, about two-thirds through. It resets the ear for the final chorus.

chips.label: Breakdown
chips.prompt: breakdown that strips back to pads and vocal, then gradually rebuilds
chips.desc: Energy drops to a few elements so the track can breathe. A staple of dance music, metalcore and pop bridges.

chips.label: Build-up
chips.prompt: eight-bar build-up with accelerating snare rolls, a rising filter sweep and a white-noise riser
chips.desc: A tension ramp into a drop or big chorus. Snare rolls double in speed and the filter opens as it climbs.

chips.label: Drop
chips.prompt: hard-hitting drop where the full bass and drums slam back in on the downbeat
chips.desc: The payoff in electronic music: the main bass hook and drums arrive at full force after the build.

chips.label: Instrumental solo
chips.prompt: instrumental solo section with the lead instrument improvising over the chorus chords
chips.desc: A spotlight for guitar, sax, keys or synth, usually after the second chorus.

chips.label: Outro / fade-out
chips.prompt: gentle outro that winds down and fades out on the main motif
chips.desc: Closes the song. Ask for a fade for radio-style endings, or a hard stop on the last downbeat for punch.

chips.label: Cold open on hook
chips.prompt: song opens cold on the chorus hook at full energy from the very first second
chips.desc: Starts with the best part. The move that holds short-form listeners before they scroll on.

chips.label: Key change, last chorus
chips.prompt: final chorus modulates up a half step for a triumphant, goosebump lift
chips.desc: The classic last-chorus truck-driver modulation. Raises energy instantly in pop ballads, gospel and boy-band anthems.

chips.label: Pop form
chips.prompt: pop song form: verse, pre-chorus, chorus, verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, final chorus
chips.desc: V-PC-C-V-PC-C-B-C. The dominant radio structure: the chorus arrives inside the first minute and returns three times.

chips.label: EDM form
chips.prompt: EDM arrangement: DJ-friendly intro, build-up, drop, breakdown, second build-up, bigger second drop, outro
chips.desc: Intro-build-drop-break-build-drop-outro. Energy moves in waves, and the beat-led intro and outro let DJs mix in and out.

chips.label: Hip-hop form
chips.prompt: hip-hop arrangement: short intro, hook, 16-bar verse, hook, second 16-bar verse, final hook
chips.desc: Intro-hook-verse-hook-verse-hook. Verses usually run 16 bars and hooks 8, so the chorus comes early and often.

chips.label: AABA standard
chips.prompt: classic 32-bar AABA form: two eight-bar A sections, a contrasting eight-bar bridge, then the A theme returns
chips.desc: The songbook form: 32 bars where the B section (the bridge) gives contrast. Standard in jazz standards, Tin Pan Alley and early rock and roll.

chips.label: 12-bar blues
chips.prompt: 12-bar blues form: four bars on the I chord, two on IV, two on I, then V, IV, I and a turnaround
chips.desc: I-I-I-I / IV-IV-I-I / V-IV-I-V. The backbone of blues, early rock and roll, boogie-woogie and a lot of jazz and funk.

chips.label: Through-composed film cue
chips.prompt: through-composed cinematic cue that evolves continuously from a quiet motif to a full climax, then resolves
chips.desc: Music built from developing sections rather than repeating verses and choruses, following a story. Used in film, trailers and game cutscenes.

chips.label: Loopable 30-second bed
chips.prompt: seamless loopable 30-second background bed with steady energy and a smooth, matching start and end
chips.desc: Even, unobtrusive music that can repeat under speech or video. Steady energy keeps the loop point invisible.

chips.label: Short 30-second hook
chips.prompt: short 30-second track built around one catchy hook that lands in the first seconds
chips.desc: Made for reels, ads and shorts: the hook is the whole song, so it arrives immediately.

chips.label: Full 3-minute song
chips.prompt: full three-minute song with an intro, two verses, choruses, a bridge and an outro
chips.desc: Flow Music songs run up to about three minutes, enough for a complete radio-length arrangement.

chips.label: Vinyl crackle
chips.prompt: warm vinyl crackle and soft surface noise running under the whole track
chips.desc: The pops and hiss of a well-loved record. Instant nostalgia for lo-fi hip-hop, boom bap and retro soul.

chips.label: Tape hiss & wow
chips.prompt: gentle cassette tape hiss with slow wow and flutter bending the pitch
chips.desc: Wow and flutter are the slow and fast pitch wobble of worn tape. Adds dreamy, unstable charm to lo-fi, chillwave and bedroom pop.

chips.label: Tape saturation
chips.prompt: warm analog tape saturation rounding off transients and thickening the low mids
chips.desc: Recording hot to tape compresses peaks and adds harmonics. It glues a mix together and makes digital sounds feel vintage.

chips.label: Warm analog
chips.prompt: warm analog production through a vintage console, soft highs and rich, rounded low end
chips.desc: The 1970s studio sound of console preamps, tape and real rooms. Flattering for soul, funk, folk and classic rock.

chips.label: Crisp modern polish
chips.prompt: crisp, polished modern mix with bright vocals, tight low end and a loud, clean master
chips.desc: Today's streaming-ready sound. Clarity and loudness for pop, K-pop, EDM and commercial hip-hop.

chips.label: Lo-fi bit-crush
chips.prompt: lo-fi bit-crushed texture with gritty 12-bit sampler grain and aliased highs
chips.desc: Reduced bit depth and sample rate, like vintage samplers. Adds grit to boom bap, chiptune, glitch and hyperpop.

chips.label: Music-box cassette
chips.prompt: music-box melody played back from a worn lo-fi cassette, wobbly and faded
chips.desc: A fragile, nostalgic texture somewhere between a lullaby and a memory. Lovely for intros, lo-fi, horror and dream pop.

chips.label: Overdriven saturated mix
chips.prompt: overdriven, saturated mix with distorted drums and bass pushed hard into the red
chips.desc: Everything clipped and crunchy on purpose. The aggressive edge of phonk, industrial, garage rock and rage beats.

chips.label: Radio / phone filter
chips.prompt: vocal filtered through a tinny AM radio or telephone band-pass, thin and crackly
chips.desc: Cuts the lows and highs so only a narrow midrange remains. Great for intros, bridges and old-time effects.

chips.label: Dry intimate close-mic
chips.prompt: dry, intimate close-miked sound where every breath and finger movement is audible
chips.desc: Very little room sound and lots of detail. Makes acoustic songs, bedroom pop and ASMR-style vocals feel right in your ear.

chips.label: Cavernous hall reverb
chips.prompt: cavernous concert-hall reverb with long, lush tails washing over everything
chips.desc: A multi-second decay that puts the music in a huge space. Suits orchestral, ambient, choral and post-rock.

chips.label: Plate reverb
chips.prompt: smooth, bright plate reverb on the vocals and snare for a classic studio sheen
chips.desc: A vibrating steel plate gives a dense, shiny reverb. The vocal sound of 1960s-70s records and still a mix staple.

chips.label: Spring reverb
chips.prompt: splashy, twangy spring reverb on guitars and drums, vintage amp style
chips.desc: The boingy reverb built into old guitar amps. Defines surf rock, rockabilly, dub and spaghetti-western tones.

chips.label: Gated 80s reverb
chips.prompt: huge gated reverb on the snare, a big explosive burst that cuts off abruptly, 1980s style
chips.desc: A big room reverb chopped short by a noise gate. The punchy, larger-than-life drum sound of 80s pop and rock.

chips.label: Shimmer reverb
chips.prompt: ethereal shimmer reverb adding octave-up halos that bloom behind the melody
chips.desc: Reverb with pitch-shifted feedback that creates a glowing, choir-like wash. Used in ambient, post-rock, worship and cinematic pop.

chips.label: Live room ambience
chips.prompt: live room ambience, the band captured playing together in a wooden studio room
chips.desc: Natural reflections from a real room, with players bleeding into each other's mics. Feels human for jazz, folk, indie and soul.

chips.label: Tape delay echoes
chips.prompt: warm tape delay echoes repeating and softly degrading after each vocal phrase
chips.desc: Echoes that darken and wobble as they repeat, like a vintage tape echo unit. Classic on vocals, guitar and dub.

chips.label: Dub delay throws
chips.prompt: dub-style delay throws on snare hits and vocal tails, spiraling into feedback echoes
chips.desc: Single hits sent into a long, filtered delay pushed toward self-oscillation. Born in Jamaican dub and now heard from reggae to techno.

chips.label: Filter sweeps
chips.prompt: slow low-pass filter sweeps opening and closing the mix for movement
chips.desc: A filter gradually reveals or hides the high frequencies. The main tension tool of house, techno and EDM builds.

chips.label: Risers and impacts
chips.prompt: white-noise risers building into deep cinematic impacts at each section change
chips.desc: Sweeping noise that climbs into a booming hit. Signals a new section in EDM, trailers and pop.

chips.label: Reverse swells
chips.prompt: reversed cymbal and reverb swells that rush into each new section
chips.desc: Sounds played backward so they grow into the downbeat. A smooth, dreamy transition effect.

chips.label: Glitch stutters
chips.prompt: glitchy stutter edits, beat repeats and chopped micro-edits on drums and vocals
chips.desc: Tiny slices repeated rapidly for a digital-error feel. Used in IDM, hyperpop, dubstep and modern pop drops.

chips.label: Chopped and screwed
chips.prompt: chopped-and-screwed treatment: slowed tempo, pitched-down vocals and skipping, repeated phrases
chips.desc: A Houston hip-hop remix style: everything slowed and lowered, with record-style cuts and repeats. Syrupy and hypnotic.

chips.label: Pitched-down half-speed
chips.prompt: pitched-down half-speed feel, heavy and syrupy with deep, slowed vocals
chips.desc: Playing audio at half speed drops it a full octave. Makes trap, phonk and dark pop feel huge and woozy.

chips.label: Sidechain pumping
chips.prompt: heavy sidechain compression making pads and bass pump in time with the kick
chips.desc: The kick ducks everything else for an instant, creating a breathing pulse. Essential in house, EDM, French house and future bass.

chips.label: Wide stereo
chips.prompt: wide stereo image with instruments spread across the field for an immersive, spacious sound
chips.desc: Doubled parts and hard panning push sounds to the far left and right. Makes choruses and pads feel enormous.

chips.label: Mono vintage
chips.prompt: vintage mono mix, everything centered and narrow like an early 1960s single
chips.desc: All instruments from one speaker, the way records were mixed before stereo. Authentic for doo-wop, early soul, rockabilly and girl-group pop.

chips.label: Punchy compressed drums
chips.prompt: punchy, heavily compressed drums with snappy transients that hit hard
chips.desc: Compression brings up the attack and body of each hit so the drums jump out in rock, hip-hop and pop.

chips.label: Heavy sub bass
chips.prompt: heavy sub-bass weight, deep low end you feel in your chest
chips.desc: Energy below 60 Hz that big systems turn into physical pressure. Core of trap, dubstep, drill and reggae sound-system culture.

chips.label: Airy sparkling highs
chips.prompt: airy, sparkling high end with shimmering detail on vocals and cymbals
chips.desc: A gentle lift above 10 kHz for a glossy, expensive sound. Flattering on pop vocals, acoustic guitars and K-pop.

chips.label: Minimal sparse arrangement
chips.prompt: minimal, sparse arrangement with lots of space around a few carefully chosen sounds
chips.desc: Fewer parts, each one featured. Lets lyrics, grooves and textures breathe in minimal techno, alt-pop and ambient.

chips.label: Dense wall of sound
chips.prompt: dense wall of sound, layered guitars, keys, strings and voices blended into one massive texture
chips.desc: Many instruments doubled and drenched in reverb until they fuse. A lush 1960s pop technique later adopted by shoegaze.

chips.label: Cinematic big mix
chips.prompt: cinematic big mix with huge dynamic range, booming low end and deep reverb
chips.desc: Quiet moments get very quiet and climaxes very loud, as in a cinema. Fits film scores, trailers and epic pop.

chips.label: Field recording rain
chips.prompt: field recording of soft rain and distant thunder underneath the music
chips.desc: Real-world texture that makes a track feel like a place. Beloved in lo-fi study beats, ambient and sleep music.

chips.label: City ambience
chips.prompt: city ambience of distant traffic, footsteps and street chatter blended under the track
chips.desc: An urban field recording that sets a night-street scene. Pairs with lo-fi, jazz-hop, trip-hop and synthwave.

chips.label: Crowd / live feel
chips.prompt: live concert feel with crowd cheers, applause and an open arena sound
chips.desc: Makes a studio track feel recorded on stage. Use it for anthems, live-band covers and festival-style drops.
